t: 2778. Sum of Squares of Special Elements
o: An element is special if its 1-indexed position divides n. Sum the squares of all special elements. For [1,2,3,4] (n=4): positions 1,2,4 divide 4, giving 1+4+16=21. For [2,7,1,19,18,3] (n=6): positions 1,2,3,6 give 4+49+1+9=63. With n ≤ 50 a direct divisibility scan is trivially sufficient.
k: Direct scan is O(n); enumerating divisors in pairs is O(√n) but unnecessary here.
Values ≤ 50 and n ≤ 50 bound the answer well below 32-bit limits (max 50·2500=125000).

a.i: Iterate 1-based i from 1 to n; whenever n % i == 0 add nums[i−1]².
s: Accumulate v*v for each divisor position.

w: Nothing tricky; the only classic mistake is mixing 0-based and 1-based indexing (position i refers to nums[i−1]). Follow-up: for huge n, enumerate divisors d ≤ √n in pairs to get O(√n).
